'''Demetri Psaltis''' ({{langx|el|Δημήτρης Ψάλτης}}) is a [[Greeks|Greek]]-[[Americans|American]] [[electrical engineer]] who was the Dean of the School of Engineering at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] from 2007 to 2017.<ref>[http://actualites.epfl.ch/presseinfo-com?id=366 NEWS EPFL :: The new face of engineering<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> Since 2024 he is a [[Emeritus|professor emeritus]] at EPFL.[https://people.epfl.ch/demetri.psaltis/?lang=en] He is one of the founders of the term and the field of [[optofluidics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.physorg.com/news596.html|title=Research on New Types of Optical Devices Modifies Optics|publisher=}}</ref> He is also well known for his past work in [[holography]], especially with regards to [[optical computing]], [[holographic data storage]], and [[neural networks]]. He is an author of over 1100 publications, contributed more than 20 book chapters, invented more than 50 patents, and currently has a [[h-index]] of [https://scholar.google.de/citations?hl=de&user=Nu_6R8sAAAAJ&view_op=list_works 105].

==Education==
Demetri Psaltis received his B.S. (1974), M.S. (1975), and Ph.D. (1977) at [[Carnegie Mellon University]].

==Academic career==
From 1980 to 2007, he worked at [[Caltech]] as an Assistant Professor (1980–1985), Associate Professor (1985–1990), Full Professor (1990–1996), Executive Officer for [[Computation and Neural Systems]] (1992–1996), Director for the National Science Foundation Center for Neuromorphic Systems Engineering (1996–1999), Thomas G. Myers Professor (1996–2007) and Director for the DARPA Center for Optofluidic Integration (2004–2007). In 2007, he moved to Switzerland as a Professor and Dean of the School of Engineering at [[EPFL]].

His past research had focused on [[optical computing]],<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Psaltis|first1=D.|title=Coherent Optical Information Systems|doi=10.1126/science.1078823|journal=Science|volume=298|issue=5597|pages=1359–1363|year=2002|pmid=12434049|bibcode=2002Sci...298.1359P|s2cid=16000569|url=http://infoscience.epfl.ch/record/155406}}</ref> [[holographic data storage]],<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Psaltis|first1=D.|last2=Buse|first2=K.|last3=Adibi|first3=A.|journal=Nature|title=Non-volatile holographic storage in doubly doped lithium niobate crystals|volume=393|issue=6686|pages=665–668|year=1998|doi=10.1038/31429|bibcode=1998Natur.393..665B|s2cid=4426548|url=http://infoscience.epfl.ch/record/155420}}</ref> [[neural networks]],<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Psaltis|first1= D.|last2=Brady|first2=D.|last3=Gu|first3=X. G.|last4=Lin|first4=S.|title=Holography in artificial neural networks|doi=10.1038/343325a0|journal=Nature|volume=343|issue=6256|pages=325–330|year=1990|pmid=2300184|bibcode=1990Natur.343..325P|s2cid= 4337012|url= http://infoscience.epfl.ch/record/155364}}</ref> [[optofluidics]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Erickson |first1=David |last2=Sinton |first2=David |last3=Psaltis |first3=Demetri |date=September 11, 2011 |title=Optofluidics for energy applications |url=http://www.nature.com/nphoton/journal/v5/n10/full/nphoton.2011.209.html |journal=[[Nature Photonics]] |volume=5 |issue=10 |pages=583–590 |bibcode=2011NaPho...5..583E |doi=10.1038/nphoton.2011.209 |s2cid=46483818|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cuennet |first1=J. G. |last2=Vasdekis |first2=A. E. |last3=De Sio |first3=L. |last4=Psaltis |first4=D. |year=2011 |title=Optofluidic modulator based on peristaltic nematogen microflows |journal=Nature Photonics |volume=5 |issue=4 |pages=234–238 |bibcode=2011NaPho...5..234C |doi=10.1038/nphoton.2011.18 |s2cid=106400512}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Psaltis |first1=D. |last2=Quake |first2=S. R. |last3=Yang |first3=C. |year=2006 |title=Developing optofluidic technology through the fusion of microfluidics and optics |url=http://infoscience.epfl.ch/record/155368 |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |volume=442 |issue=7101 |pages=381–386 |bibcode=2006Natur.442..381P |doi=10.1038/nature05060 |pmid=16871205 |s2cid=1729058}}</ref> and on [[nonlinear optics]] particularly in scattering media.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Yaqoob |first1=Z. |last2=Psaltis |first2=D. |last3=Feld |first3=M. S. |last4=Yang |first4=C. |year=2008 |title=Optical phase conjugation for turbidity suppression in biological samples |journal=Nature Photonics |volume=2 |issue=2 |pages=110–115 |bibcode=2008NaPho...2..110Y |doi=10.1038/nphoton.2007.297 |pmc=2688902 |pmid=19492016}}</ref>

His current research focuses on optical computing for neural networks<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wetzstein |first1=Gordon |last2=Ozcan |first2=Aydogan |last3=Gigan |first3=Sylvain |last4=Fan |first4=Shanhui |last5=Englund |first5=Dirk |last6=Soljačić |first6=Marin |last7=Denz |first7=Cornelia |last8=Miller |first8=David A.
